config.title: Design DataTable API

intro.title: Design DataTable API
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable DataTable component in React with TypeScript. You'll learn how to design a component API by defining props that control the table's data, columns, and key behaviors. The core concept is using TypeScript interfaces to create a strict, type-safe contract for the component's inputs. You'll work with React functional components, JSX for structure, and TypeScript generics to make the table flexible for different data types. By the end, you'll have a customizable table component that can display any dataset you provide.
intro.usecase: A well-designed DataTable API is a cornerstone of enterprise dashboards and admin panels, such as those in analytics tools like Google Analytics or CRM systems like Salesforce. Developers use these APIs to build interactive tables that support sorting by columns, filtering by user input, and pagination for large datasets—common in e-commerce order management or financial reporting interfaces. Implementing a clean, type-safe API in React with TypeScript ensures that these complex UI components are maintainable, predictable, and easy to extend as product requirements evolve, directly impacting developer productivity and end-user experience.

objectives: Implement a TypeScript interface to define the structure of a DataTable component's props.
Construct a DataTable component that accepts and renders data based on the defined API.
Configure the DataTable to conditionally display a loading state when data is being fetched.
Initialize and manage local state within the DataTable to handle user interactions like row selection.
Bind event handlers to user interface elements within the DataTable to control actions such as sorting.
Manipulate and transform the data array passed to the DataTable to enable features like pagination.
Integrate the DataTable component into a parent application and pass the required data and configuration props.

steps.title: Import React and define TypeScript interfaces for DataTable
steps.instruction: Import React from 'react' and define two TypeScript interfaces: one named 'Column' with properties 'key' (string) and 'title' (string), and another named 'DataTableProps' with properties 'columns' (array of Column) and 'data' (array of objects with any keys).
steps.hint: Start with 'import React from "react"' then use 'interface Column' and 'interface DataTableProps' to define the types.

steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have React imported and two TypeScript interfaces defined: Column and DataTableProps.
successCriteria: React is imported from 'react', and both Column and DataTableProps interfaces are defined with the specified properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Add basic table structure with headers
steps.instruction: Inside your DataTable component, return a <table> element with a <thead> section that maps over the columns prop to create header cells.
steps.hint: Use the columns array from props to generate <th> elements inside <thead>. Remember to add a key prop to each header cell.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a table with a header row containing cells for each column title.
successCriteria: The DataTable component returns a <table> element with a <thead> that maps over columns to create <th> elements with proper keys.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're mapping over the columns prop and returning <th> elements with keys inside <thead>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The table structure or header mapping isn't quite correct. Review how to map arrays in JSX and the required table HTML structure.

steps.title: Add table body with data rows
steps.instruction: Inside the DataTable component, add a <tbody> element after the <thead> that maps over the data prop to create table rows. Each row should contain a <td> cell for each column, displaying the corresponding value from the data object.
steps.hint: Use the data prop (an array of objects) and the columns prop (an array with keys) to generate rows and cells. For each row, map over columns to create cells using column.key to access the value from the row object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The table will have a body section with rows of data, each row containing cells that display the values from the data objects, aligned with the column keys.
successCriteria: A <tbody> element is added inside the <table> that maps over the data prop to create <tr> rows, and each row maps over columns to create <td> cells displaying data[row][column.key].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a <tbody> or started mapping over data, but check that each row correctly maps over columns to create <td> cells with the proper data values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The table body or data rows are missing or incorrectly structured. Ensure you add a <tbody> that maps over data to create rows, and within each row, map over columns to create cells using column.key.

steps.title: Add optional loading state prop
steps.instruction: Add an optional isLoading prop to the DataTableProps interface and include it in the DataTable component's parameter list.
steps.hint: Use TypeScript's optional property syntax (?) in the interface and add isLoading to the component's destructured props.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTableProps interface now includes an optional isLoading property, and the DataTable component's parameter list includes isLoading.
successCriteria: DataTableProps interface has an optional isLoading property and the DataTable component's parameter list includes isLoading.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure isLoading is optional in the interface and included in the component's props.
steps.feedbackWrong: The isLoading prop is missing or not correctly added as optional. Check the interface and component parameter list.

steps.title: Implement loading state UI
steps.instruction: Inside the DataTable component, add conditional rendering to show a loading message when the isLoading prop is true. Use a ternary operator to conditionally render either the loading message or the existing table.
steps.hint: Check if isLoading is true. If true, return a loading message element. Otherwise, return the existing table.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTable component will show a loading message when isLoading is true, and show the table when isLoading is false.
successCriteria: The component uses conditional rendering with a ternary operator to check the isLoading prop and return either a loading message or the table.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your conditional rendering logic. Make sure you're using a ternary operator to return either the loading message or the table based on the isLoading prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional rendering for the loading state isn't implemented correctly. Review how to use ternary operators in JSX to conditionally render different content.

steps.title: Add empty state handling
steps.instruction: Add conditional logic to display a message when the data array is empty and the component is not loading.
steps.hint: Check if the data array length is 0 and isLoading is false, then return a message like 'No data available'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will show a message when there's no data instead of an empty table.
successCriteria: The component returns a message when data is empty and not loading.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented empty state handling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure to check both conditions: data length is 0 and isLoading is false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The empty state logic is missing or incorrect. Try adding an if statement before the table return.

steps.title: Add row click handler prop
steps.instruction: Add an optional onRowClick prop to the DataTableProps interface. The prop should be a function that receives the row data and row index as parameters and returns void.
steps.hint: Extend the existing DataTableProps interface with a new property. Use TypeScript to define the function signature.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTableProps interface now includes an optional onRowClick callback prop with proper TypeScript typing.
successCriteria: DataTableProps interface has an optional onRowClick property typed as (row: Record<string, any>, index: number) => void
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added onRowClick, but check the function signature. It should accept row data and index parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onRowClick prop is missing or incorrectly typed. Add it to DataTableProps with proper TypeScript function signature.

steps.title: Add optional className prop for styling
steps.instruction: Add an optional 'className' prop to the DataTableProps interface and apply it to the table element's className attribute.
steps.hint: Extend the interface with 'className?: string' and add it to the table element like <table className={className}>.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTable component now accepts an optional className prop that can be used to apply custom CSS classes to the table element.
successCriteria: The DataTableProps interface includes 'className?: string' and the table element has 'className={className}' attribute.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the className prop but might have missed applying it to the table element or the interface definition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The className prop wasn't properly added. Check that you've extended the interface and applied it to the table element.
